**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — no redline.**

Section 17(b) lets Sparkling terminate at any time on 90 days' written notice with no early-termination fee, and Section 17(a) makes the term open-ended rather than a committed multi-year lock-in. Garman has no convenience right at all — it can exit only on insolvency events or uncured material default under Section 17(c), which is better than our fallback allows.

Two minor gaps versus the preferred position, noted but not flagged: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a convenience termination (refunds appear only on rejection under Section 8 and on Garman default under Section 17(c)). Worth picking up only if Section 17 is reopened for other reasons.
